segments.arabic:
١١٠٧٠- حوّاء بنت يزيد
بن سنان بن كرز بن زعوراء بن عبد الأشهل «١» الأنصارية، ذكرها أبو عمر، فقال:
قال مصعب الزبيري: أسلمت، وكانت، تكتم زوجها قيس بن الخطيم الشاعر إسلامها، فلما قدم قيس مكة حين خرجوا يطلبون الحلف من قريش عرض عليه رسول اللَّه ﷺ الإسلام، فاستنظره قيس حتى يقدم المدينة، فسأله رسول اللَّه ﷺ أن يجتنب زوجته حوّاء بنت يزيد، وأوصاه بها خيرا، وقال له: إنها قد أسلمت، فقبل قيس وصية رسول اللَّه ﷺ، فبلغ ذلك رسول اللَّه ﷺ فقال: وفي الأديعج.
قال أبو عمر: أنكرت هذه القصة على مصعب، وقال منكرها: إن صاحبها قيس بن شماس. وأما قيس بن الخطيم فقتل قبل الهجرة. والقول عندنا قول مصعب، وقيس بن شماس أسنّ من قيس بن الخطيم، ولم يدرك الإسلام، إنما أدركه ولده ثابت بن قيس.
انتهى.
وقد وافق مصعب العدويّ، فقال: حوّاء بنت يزيد بن سنان بن كرز بن زعوراء بن عبد الأشهل زوج قيس بن الخطيم، ولدت له ابنه ثابت بن قيس.
وقال محمّد بن سلّام الجمحيّ صاحب «طبقات الشّعراء»: أسلمت امرأة قيس بن الخطيم، وكان يقال لها حوّاء وكان يصدّها عن الإسلام، ويعبث بها، وهي ساجدة فيقلبها على رأسها، وكان رسول اللَّه ﷺ وهو بمكة قبل الهجرة يخبر عن أمر الأنصار، فأخبر بإسلامها وبما تلقى من قيس، فلما كان الموسم أتاه النبي ﷺ فقال: «إنّ امرأتك قد أسلمت وإنّك تؤذيها، فأحبّ أنّك لا تتعرّض لها» .
وسبق إلى ذلك محمّد بن إسحاق، فذكره في «السّيرة النّبويّة» قال: حدثني عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة نحو هذا، وزاد: وكان سعد بن معاذ خال حوّاء لأنّ أمها عقرب بنت معاذ، فأسلمت حواء، فحسن إسلامها، وكان زوجها قيس على كفره، فكان يدخل عليها فيراها تصلّي فيأخذ ثيابها فيضعها على رأسها، ويقول: إنك لتدينين دينا لا يدري ما هو؟ وذكر أنّ النبيّ ﷺ أوصاه بها نحو ما تقدم، فهذا كله يقوّي كلام مصعب. ويحمل على أن قيسا قتل في تلك السنة، فإن الأنصار اجتمعوا بالنبيّ ﷺ ثلاث مرات بعقبة مني، ففي الأولى كانوا قليلا جدا، ورجعوا مسلمين يختفون بإسلامهم، فأسلم جماعة من أكرمهم خفية، ثم في
(١) أسد الغابة ت ٦٨٦٤، الاستيعاب ت ٣٣٥٢.
segments.english:
11070—Hawwa bint Yazid

ibn Sinan ibn Kurz ibn Za'ura ibn 'Abd al-Ashhal,¹ the Ansari woman. Abu 'Umar mentioned her and said:

Mus'ab al-Zubayri said: She embraced Islam but concealed her Islam from her husband, Qays ibn al-Khatim, the poet. When Qays came to Mecca, at the time when they had gone out to seek Quraysh's alliance, the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—offered Islam to him. Qays asked him to allow him time until he returned to Medina. The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—asked him to leave his wife, Hawwa bint Yazid, alone, commended her to his good care, and told him, “She has embraced Islam.” Qays accepted the counsel of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When this reached the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—he said, “al-Uday'ij (‘the little dark-eyed one’) has kept his word.”

Abu 'Umar said: This story was objected to in Mus'ab's account. The one who rejected it said, “The man concerned was Qays ibn Shammas. As for Qays ibn al-Khatim, he was killed before the Hijra.” In our view, however, Mus'ab's statement is correct. Qays ibn Shammas was older than Qays ibn al-Khatim and did not live to see Islam; it was only his son, Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who lived to see it.

End of quotation.

al-'Adawi agreed with Mus'ab, saying: Hawwa bint Yazid ibn Sinan ibn Kurz ibn Za'ura ibn 'Abd al-Ashhal was the wife of Qays ibn al-Khatim, and she bore him his son, Thabit ibn Qays ibn al-Khatim.

Muhammad ibn Sallam al-Jumahi, the author of Tabaqat al-Shu'ara, said: Qays ibn al-Khatim's wife embraced Islam. She was called Hawwa. He used to turn her away from Islam and mistreat her; while she was prostrating, he would turn her upside down onto her head. While the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was in Mecca before the Hijra, he would receive reports about the affairs of the Ansar. He was informed of her conversion to Islam and of what she suffered at Qays's hands. When the pilgrimage season arrived, the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—came to him and said, “Your wife has embraced Islam, and you are harming her. I would like you not to interfere with her.”

Muhammad ibn Ishaq had already related this in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya. He said: 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatada related to me something similar to this, adding: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was Hawwa's maternal uncle, because her mother was 'Aqrab bint Mu'adh. Hawwa embraced Islam, and her commitment to Islam was excellent, while her husband, Qays ibn al-Khatim, remained an unbeliever. He would enter upon her and see her praying, whereupon he would take her clothes and place them over her head, saying, “You are indeed professing a religion whose nature no one knows?” He also mentioned that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—commended her to Qays's care, approximately as related above. All of this strengthens Mus'ab's account. It may be understood as meaning that Qays was killed during that same year, for the Ansar met the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—three times at al-'Aqaba in Mina. At the first meeting they were very few indeed. They returned as Muslims, concealing their Islam, and a group of their noblest people secretly embraced Islam. Then, in—

segments.arabic:
السنة الثانية بايعوا النبيّ ﷺ بيعة العقبة، وهي الأولى، وكانوا اثني عشر رجلا ورجعوا، فانتشر الإسلام، وكثر بالمدينة ثم بايعوا البيعة الثانية وهم اثنان وسبعون رجلا وامرأتان، فكأنّ إسلام حوّاء هذه كان بين الأولى والثانية ووصية قيس في الثانية، فقتل بين الثانية والثالثة. واللَّه أعلم.
ووقع لابن مندة في هذه والتي قبلها وهم، فإنه قال: حوّاء بنت زيد بن السكن الأشهلية امرأة قيس بن الخطيم، يقال لها أم بجيد، ثم ساق حديث أم بجيد المذكورة في التي بعد هذه، وفيه تخليط، فإن أم بجيد اسم والدها زيد بغير ياء قبل الزاي، وجدها السكن، وأما امرأة قيس فاسم والدها يزيد بزيادة الياء، واسم جدها سنان.
segments.english:
In the second year, they pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the Pledge of al-Aqaba—which was the first pledge. They numbered twelve men, and they returned; Islam then spread and became widespread in Medina. Thereafter, they gave the second pledge, when they numbered seventy-two men and two women. It therefore appears that this Hawa embraced Islam between the first and second [meetings], that the charge concerning her was given to Qays at the second, and that he was killed between the second and third. Allah knows best.

Ibn Manda fell into an error concerning this woman and the woman preceding her. He said: “Hawa bint Zayd ibn al-Sakan al-Ashhaliyya, the wife of Qays ibn al-Khatim, is said to have been called Umm Bujayd.” He then cited the hadith of Umm Bujayd mentioned in the entry following this one. This contains confusion: the name of Umm Bujayd's father was Zayd, without a ya before the letter zay, and her grandfather was al-Sakan; as for the wife of Qays, her father's name was Yazid, with the additional ya, and her grandfather's name was Sinan.
